claims.text: Integrating machine learning with CALPHAD will improve the accuracy of determining transition temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity relative to experiments, DFT free-energy studies, and TOR-TILD.
Integrating machine learning with CALPHAD will improve the efficiency of determining the specified transition and dense-fluid thermodynamic properties.
Machine learning can efficiently screen high-entropy-alloy composition spaces.
Machine learning can predict the thermodynamic properties needed to locate the solid-to-dense-fluid transition.
CALPHAD can represent complicated multicomponent phase behavior using thermodynamic databases developed from lower-order binary and ternary systems.
CALPHAD extrapolation provides a reliable account of higher-order multicomponent systems.
Combining machine learning with CALPHAD is sufficient to retain the accuracy needed for solid and dense-fluid transition thermodynamics.
Configurational entropy and thermodynamic properties act as mediators between the proposed intervention and the predicted transition-property improvements.
The accuracy of machine-learning models for high-entropy materials depends strongly on the size and quality of the training dataset.
The vast compositional space of high-entropy alloys makes conventional lengthy, costly, high-fidelity screening difficult.
The proposed approach is limited to multicomponent high-entropy materials in high-temperature states.
